_meta.status: DRAFT for approval - proposed per-category story modules
_meta.purpose: Replace the single global story/Flow template with one module per category. Backend must load the module by category id (1-10). Never parse categories from free text; use this table.
how_backend_should_use_it: 3. Merge with 'global_rules' (language, scene timing, dialogue rules).
4. Build the scene-by-scene story using story_beats in order (one beat per scene).
5. Build each Flow script using that category's flow_script_rules, NOT a shared boilerplate.
6. Run 'anti_repetition' check against the last stories before showing output.

global_rules.language: Roman Urdu only for dialogue and all agent replies
dialogue_style: Sentence case, simple spoken Roman Urdu
Do not use the word 'turant'; use 'usi waqt' or 'isi waqt'
global_rules.no_invented_numbers: Never invent statistics, results or prices. Use only what research actually found.
global_rules.free_first: Prefer free or open-source tools; mention paid tools only with a trial or alternative.

continuity_lock_rules.fixed_line_format: CONTINUITY LOCK: Use the character selected in Flow for tag @WM25-X exactly as set (same face, hairstyle, beard length and shape, moustache, chin/goatee style, body build and wardrobe). Do not restyle or alter the character in any way. Use the same character voice as set in Flow, identical in every scene. Keep the same studio look as set in Flow (same room, same wall colors, same desk, same lighting style). Do not move the scene to a different room.
continuity_lock_rules.placement: Appended to [PRESENTER & ACTION] block in every scene's Flow script without modifying existing presenter text
continuity_lock_rules.rule_1_tag: @WM25-X must be the actual selected character tag of that story (e.g. @WM25-5 or @WM25-1). Never mix tags inside one story.
continuity_lock_rules.rule_2_locked_elements: The three locked elements are: (a) studio look, (b) character face and wardrobe, (c) character voice. These must never change from scene to scene.
continuity_lock_rules.rule_3_scene_visual_props: Story-based variation is allowed ONLY inside the [SCENE VISUAL & PROPS] block, and only as a change of environment inside the same studio, for example: show the demonstration on the back wall, on the left wall, on a hologram screen in front of the presenter, or change props on the desk. The room itself, its style and lighting must stay the same.
continuity_lock_rules.rule_4_director_camera_lighting: The [DIRECTOR CAMERA & LIGHTING] block must not describe a different room or a different lighting setup than the locked studio. Camera angle and movement may vary, the studio look may not.
continuity_lock_rules.rule_5_mode_a_voice: Mode A (screen-only) scenes: keep the same voice-over character voice. No new voice.
continuity_lock_rules.rule_6_preservation: Do NOT edit or rename the Presenter block itself. Only append the CONTINUITY LOCK line.

visual_signature_fields: opening line of the Flow script
anti_repetition.rule: Store the visual signature of the last 5 stories. A new story must differ from each of the last 3 in at least 3 of the 6 fields. If not, regenerate the Flow blocks (not the dialogue).
anti_repetition.forbidden: Do not start every Flow script with the same sentence. Do not reuse the same camera/lighting/presenter block word-for-word across videos.

sequence_order: 10. Live Showdown (Method A vs Method B)
script_pattern_rotation.lahori_punjab_voice_dna: Authentic, engaging Lahori / Pakistani Punjab conversational tone across all patterns — relatable, punchy, warm elder-brother/friend cadence with mid-story Scene 5 Interesting Factor spike and binge-watch series bridge.
script_pattern_rotation.demo_opening_rule: Any pattern classified as a Demo (Seedha Demo, TikTok trickdemo, Speedrun Challenge Demo) MUST strictly begin Scene 1 with a topic-identifying question or hook dialogue clearly indicating the topic to spark curiosity BEFORE transitioning directly into hands-on demonstration steps in Scene 2+.
script_pattern_rotation.uniqueness_rule: Every generated story must carry a unique tone, angle, and dialogue compared to recent stories while staying aligned with the topic requirements and category.

module_types.standard_tutorial: One topic, one video, 10 scenes, self-contained.
module_types.ongoing_series: Never-ending part-by-part series (Part 1, 2, 3...). Each part links to the previous one. Runs under its own extended-length test format already defined in the agent file.
module_types.ideas_only: Only ideas and possibilities, no hands-on step-by-step.
module_types.lecture_series: Course style, chapter by chapter, 16:9, Lecture Series Format.
module_types.custom: Topic supplied directly by the user, outside the regular rotation.

categories.name: AI & Smart Technology
categories.story_angle: Explain what a new AI or smart-tech development means for an ordinary Pakistani viewer and what they can do with it today.
story_beats: Hook: surprising claim about the AI/smart tech
What it is in one simple sentence
Why it matters to a normal viewer
categories.visual_mode: Presenter on Hook and CTA; middle scenes mix concept visuals and short screen proof.

flow_script_rules.camera: Smooth gliding or orbiting shots; vary between medium and close; avoid repeating the same push-in every video.
flow_script_rules.lighting_and_set: Modern smart-lab or clean studio; colour scheme chosen per story (not always navy + cyan/amber).
flow_script_rules.presenter_action: Explaining gestures, pointing at concept visuals.
flow_script_rules.hologram: Allowed, used once or twice at most, only when explaining the core concept.

categories.dialogue_tone: Curious, clear, slightly excited; explain jargon in one line.
categories.cta_style: Ask which use viewers would try first.
categories.thumbnail_style: Strong concept visual; wow factor from background, minimal text.

categories.name: AI Chatbots, Workflows & AI Tools
categories.story_angle: Show one concrete task done with a chatbot or AI tool (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI tools, Google Flow, Nano) or a small workflow built from them.
story_beats: Hook: task that normally takes long, done fast
categories.visual_mode: Demonstration mode: presenter only on Hook and CTA; middle scenes are full-screen screen recording of the tool with voiceover.

flow_script_rules.camera: Screen-recording framing with cursor focus and zoom-ins on the exact button or setting; presenter scenes use a stable medium shot.
flow_script_rules.lighting_and_set: Clean desk setup with monitor glow; keep it practical, not cinematic sci-fi.
flow_script_rules.presenter_action: Pointing toward the screen, nodding, short explanation gestures.
flow_script_rules.hologram: Not used in middle scenes; optional tiny accent in Hook only.

categories.dialogue_tone: Instructor-friendly, step by step, no hype.
categories.cta_style: Ask which tool or task to cover next.
categories.thumbnail_style: Tool logo area + result preview, short headline.

categories.name: AI Prompt Hacks & Shortcuts
categories.story_angle: One prompt technique or image+prompt workflow, shown with a weak prompt vs strong prompt and the visible difference in output.
story_beats: Hook: same AI, two very different results
The weak prompt and its poor result
The hack named in one line
How to write the improved prompt
categories.visual_mode: Presenter on Hook and CTA; middle scenes are split view of prompt text and generated output.

flow_script_rules.camera: Static or slow lateral movement over prompt and output panels; cut quickly between before and after.
flow_script_rules.lighting_and_set: Bright, minimal creator desk; prompt text legible on screen.
flow_script_rules.presenter_action: Typing, comparing two outputs, thumbs-up gesture.

categories.dialogue_tone: Playful, smart, 'trick' feeling, short punchy sentences.
categories.cta_style: Ask viewers to comment their prompt.

categories.name: PC & Windows Hacks

series.format_note: Stand-alone complete 10-scene tutorial format: exactly 10 scenes from Hook to Conclusion + Save CTA with zero next-part promises.

categories.story_angle: Windows hidden tools, settings, CMD and PowerShell tricks to fix real PC problems (slow PC, temp files, hidden settings, command-line tools) or any other method found via research.
categories.visual_mode: Demonstration mode: presenter on Hook and CTA; middle scenes full-screen Windows screen recording, with CMD or PowerShell close-ups when commands are used.

flow_script_rules.camera: Screen recording with zoom on menus, terminal text and click targets; slow zoom-out when showing results.
flow_script_rules.lighting_and_set: Practical PC desk or laptop setup for presenter scenes.
flow_script_rules.presenter_action: Pointing at screen, cautious 'be careful' gesture for safety note.

categories.hook_style: Hook: direct PC problem with zero invented numbers.
categories.cta_style: Conclusion + Save CTA in Scene 10 only; topic complete in one video with zero next-part promises.
categories.thumbnail_style: Windows screen with highlighted fix and part number.
categories.duplicate_check_scope: Same fix; new part must add something new.

categories.name: New Technology & Product Tutorials
categories.story_angle: New launch, new feature or new product: what is new, who it is for, and how to try or use it.
story_beats: What is new compared to before
How to try or access it
categories.visual_mode: Presenter on Hook, verdict and CTA; middle scenes show product visuals or the interface.

flow_script_rules.camera: News-desk style medium shots; product close-ups and interface walk-throughs.
flow_script_rules.lighting_and_set: Tech news studio, neutral cool tones with one accent colour that changes per story.
flow_script_rules.presenter_action: Holding or presenting the product concept, confident news-anchor posture.
flow_script_rules.hologram: Optional once for product concept; not default.

categories.cta_style: Ask if viewers will try it.
categories.thumbnail_style: Product name headline over product visual.

categories.name: Future Tech & Positive Breakthroughs
categories.story_angle: Useful upcoming technology or major beneficial developments; optimistic but honest about timelines.
categories.visual_mode: Concept visuals dominate; presenter on Hook and CTA only.

flow_script_rules.camera: Cinematic wide shots and slow reveals of concept visuals.
flow_script_rules.lighting_and_set: Hopeful bright or warm futuristic tones; avoid dark cyber look.

categories.cta_style: Ask what future tech viewers want in Pakistan.

categories.name: Secrets (WhatsApp, Google, Google Chrome, Google Maps, Gmail, Google Drive, Google Play Store, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, Telegram, Windows, ChatGPT, Google Gemini, CapCut)

series.format_note: Ongoing, never-ending part-by-part series covering hidden settings and features in major daily-used apps that normal users do not know about.

categories.story_angle: One hidden setting or feature in one specific app, shown on a phone or app screen.
story_beats: Hook: teaser of the hidden trick (app name + part number)
CTA question in comments + next part teaser
categories.visual_mode: Presenter on Hook and CTA; middle scenes are phone or app screen recording with tap highlights.

flow_script_rules.camera: Phone-screen framing, finger tap highlights, quick zoom into the exact menu; occasional over-shoulder shot.
flow_script_rules.lighting_and_set: Casual bright desk, phone prominent; mood 'insider secret'.
flow_script_rules.presenter_action: Whisper-like lean-in gesture for secrets, holding phone.

categories.dialogue_tone: Insider, 'kisi ko nahi pata' energy, quick and friendly.
categories.cta_style: High-engagement question in comments and next part teaser.
categories.duplicate_check_scope: Same app + same feature; rotate apps across parts.

categories.name: Income & Skills: Tools That Earn
categories.story_angle: Ideas only: how viewers could build income with tools, skills and platforms. No step-by-step tutorials, no income promises.
story_beats: Hook: the idea in one line
What skill or tool is needed (free first)
How the idea can earn (no guarantees)
First small step viewers can take
categories.visual_mode: Presenter-led idea storytelling with simple idea cards or visuals; no hands-on screen walkthrough.

flow_script_rules.camera: Warm medium shots, idea cards appearing beside the presenter.

categories.dialogue_tone: Motivating but realistic; never claim guaranteed earnings.
categories.cta_style: Ask which idea viewers want detailed next.
categories.thumbnail_style: Idea headline with simple icon visuals.
categories.duplicate_check_scope: Same idea; ideas-only, no overlap with tutorial categories.
